reason: Three upstream packages use Node's built-in synchronous SQLite binding for an optional session store, the FTS5 session search and a key-value backend; they need WAL with full sync, a busy timeout, savepoints, triggers, STRICT tables, identity pragmas and FTS5 with unicode61 and highlight(). The Go store uses modernc.org/sqlite through database/sql behind one driver package, provisional until the measurements in the spec are taken.

Product source uses Node streams as the type of process and socket ends, as in-process pipes (PassThrough), for drain-based backpressure, for pipeline and finished, and to bridge Node and web streams. Go has one stream model: io.Reader and io.Writer with blocking writes, io.Pipe and io.Copy, plus stated bounds and close-on-cancel rules.

Product source uses EventEmitter in two classes, once() to wait for an event in two places and addAbortListener in six. Between components the Go design uses cordis typed events; inside a component a channel closed once plus an error accessor, select on ctx.Done(), and context.AfterFunc.

Buffer is used (mostly as a global) to hold and join bytes, count the bytes of a string, and encode utf8, base64, base64url, hex and utf16le; isUtf8 and the platform size constants appear in three files. Go uses []byte, len, encoding/base64, encoding/hex, unicode/utf8 and unicode/utf16, and every size limit names its unit.

Outside tests the imports are parseArgs (44 files, all scripts), promisify (25, mostly scripts), isDeepStrictEqual (18 product files), inspect (12), and single uses of parseEnv, getSystemErrorName and types. Go uses a per-type equality rule, fmt and log/slog for diagnostics, and syscall.Errno; promisify and the type predicates have no counterpart because Go calls block and values are typed.

StringDecoder is imported by the SDK line transport and one release script, to decode UTF-8 that arrives split across chunks; the same need is met elsewhere by TextDecoder in streaming mode, setEncoding and hand-written trimming. The Go design splits protocols on bytes and decodes whole frames, and uses one incremental decoder where text must be shown before a frame ends.

AsyncLocalStorage carries the initiating agent in core/agent, the current query activity in the SDK server, a re-entrancy flag in hmr, the current evaluation inside the Node program runner, and a flag for an HTTP client workaround. Each use maps to a context.Context value or an explicit parameter, or exists only inside Node-specific code; none needs storage attached to a goroutine.

In product source node:assert guards internal invariants in hmr, timeline and the computer-use clients; every other import is a test, fixture or script. In Go a broken invariant is a returned error or a contained panic, and tests use the testing package.

The files that import node:process by name are governance and release scripts; the same object is a global used for arguments, environment, platform, exit and standard streams. Go reads these through os, runtime and os/signal, with process starting specified in libs/node-process-builtins.md.

Exists only because of Node: the single use (experimental/liveshare relay-h2-idle.ts:85) listens to the channel on which Node's undici HTTP client announces sockets, to swallow an idle-timeout error that client reports on a socket no request owns. Go's net/http returns connection errors to the request's caller.

Exists only because of Node: the single use (ptc-runtime-node scoped-repl-evaluator.ts:44) catches errors thrown later by callbacks of a model-written JavaScript program inside the Node runner process. The Go host never evaluates JavaScript in process; a program runner is a separate process and reports a failed evaluation over its connection.

Exists only because the upstream host is JavaScript: webworker-runtime bundles this npm copy of node:buffer so that host code can run in a browser Web Worker. A Go program uses []byte from the language, including when compiled to WebAssembly.

Exists only because the upstream host is JavaScript: webworker-runtime bundles this npm copy of node:stream (implemented/stream.ts:9) so that host code can run in a browser Web Worker. Go's io package is part of the standard library on every target.

Exists only because the upstream host is JavaScript: webworker-runtime bundles this npm copy of node:string_decoder (implemented/string_decoder.ts:4) so that host code can run in a browser Web Worker. The Go decoding rule is specified under node:string_decoder and needs no polyfill.

Used once, for the default colour level of the vendored console log exporter (vendor/logger-console/src/index.ts:23), which is not ported. What remains is a rule for any Go code that writes colour: only to a terminal, only when NO_COLOR is unset and TERM is not dumb, never to a protocol stream.

title: Incremental reads of process output decode from an arbitrary byte offset, so a character split across two reads becomes two replacement characters

reason: The Go output reader uses the shared incremental decoder: it holds back an incomplete trailing character, reports offsets that count only emitted bytes, and starts retained windows on a character boundary (DH-LIB-NODEPLATFORM-R5 and -R6).

title: SQLite driver for the session store, search index and machine state: modernc.org/sqlite through database/sql, pure Go, provisional until measured
license: BSD-3-Clause (embeds SQLite, public domain, and sqlite-vec, MIT)
verified: go list -m -json, go list -m -versions, go mod download -json, LICENSE files, doc.go, driver.go and lib/ read in module cache, 2026-11-18

title: A pure-Go SQLite driver, accepted on measurement, with a fixed fallback order
One package owns the driver; everything else sees database/sql behind the store interface
Search tokenization uses only what stock FTS5 has; language handling is done in Go
The binary builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 for every release target, the libc pin matches, and the notices list the driver
No file outside the driver package imports a SQLite driver
The store contract suite passes on each pure-Go driver: snapshots, savepoints, append-only triggers, a contiguous prefix after a kill
A second process waits, then gets the classified busy error; an in-process open and close of the database file does not strip its locks
Cancellation interrupts a slow statement, a live backup is consistent, and a foreign or newer database is refused unchanged
A multilingual search corpus returns the expected hits, identically on both pure-Go drivers
Each SQLite result code maps to its harness error on each driver
Benchmarks for flush, large payloads, indexing, search, cancellation, two processes and binary size, recorded per operating system and driver
Streams, events, bytes, text decoding and per-call state: the Go standard library, cordis typed events and one incremental UTF-8 decoder
Split on bytes, decode whole frames, and use one incremental decoder where a frame cannot be waited for
State that follows a call chain is a context value or a parameter; there is no goroutine-local storage
Every chunking of a byte corpus decodes to the same text; strict mode reports the first invalid byte
A line protocol fed one byte at a time decodes correctly; an over-long line is a classified error
Every size cut lands on a character boundary and adds no replacement character
A stalled consumer keeps memory under the buffer limit and triggers the declared overflow rule
Cancellation releases every blocked reader and leaves no goroutine; a stop function removes its callback
Attribution nests, follows the context into goroutines, and is absent from detached work
Lifecycle channels close once, equality follows each type's rule, and printed secrets are redacted
Colour is written only to a terminal without NO_COLOR, and never to a protocol stream
